brief-1.text: Identifies the September 7 courier change as the trigger: Ridgeway and Millbrook samples now wait hours for a single 3:30 pm pickup. Supported by the onset date, the two clinics producing 83% of flags from about 30% of volume, and the before-11-am (11%) vs after-1-pm (about 1%) split, which tracks waiting time. Harbour is on the same courier but spins on site and is barely affected.

Names the mechanism as refrigeration of unspun whole blood. Under the August 1 cold-hold policy, long waits now mean hours in the fridge, and cold stops the cells' sodium-potassium pump, so potassium leaks into the serum (pseudohyperkalemia). The reply must not clear the cold-hold policy because it predates the onset. It became harmful only once waits got long. The fix is to centrifuge before cold hold, or hold unspun blood at room temperature, or restore frequent pickups. Saying only 'transport delay' misses this key.

Rules out or strongly weakens the Analyzer A reagent lot. Flagged samples split 57/43 across analyzers, matching A's roughly 60% share of volume. Inpatient and ED flag rates on the same analyzers are unchanged. The QC shift is small and inside limits. Quarantining the lot should not be recommended as the fix.

Rules out or strongly weakens the new phlebotomist and hemolysis. The hemolysis index is normal on 93% of flagged samples. Millbrook, which had no staff change, is affected almost as much as Ridgeway. Onset was September 8, not September 1. Normal calcium also argues against EDTA contamination. Retraining Tomas is not the fix.

brief-2.text: Identifies phantom (paper) shrink from a receiving quantity mismatch. Greenfold pallets hold 50 bags (five layers of ten), but scanning a pallet books the item-master quantity of 60, so every Greenfold pallet overstates book stock by 10 bags (one sixth). The stock count then shows this as shrink. That is why it sits in bagged landscape and only in the six stores on Greenfold delivery since July 8. 'Nobody edited the item master' is the problem, not an exoneration.

Rules out self-checkout. The three southern self-checkout stores are flat at 1.4%, the kiosks went in during May with no matching shift, and the loss sits in 20–40 kg bags, not the small items typical of self-checkout loss. Pulling the kiosks (about £90k) is not justified.

Rules out the security contractor change. Eight stores switched, so three switched stores outside the affected six show no rise, and one affected store didn't switch at all. Reverting the contract (about £90k) is not justified.

Rules out or heavily discounts organised theft. Power tools are only 7% of the extra shrink and within 2% of book at four of six stores. Large-scale theft of heavy compost and gravel bags is implausible. The reply should recommend the cheap check first: count bags on arriving Greenfold pallets, or reconcile booked receipts against Greenfold invoices or delivery notes, then fix the pack quantity and restate inventory.

brief-3.text: Identifies the October 3 IVR change as the cause. With the date-of-birth and postcode prompts gone, and verification rules unchanged, agents must now collect and check ID on every call. That adds a near-constant ~1.8 minutes of talk time at the start of every call, which matches QA's finding that the extra time is in the opening minutes. The fix is to restore or redesign automated verification, not to add staff. (Lower IVR abandonment also sends more calls to agents, which worsens answer times.)

Rules out the new hires. Tenured agents rose by the same 1.7–1.9 minutes. Arithmetically, 18 of about 140 agents running about a minute slower moves the average by only ~0.1–0.15 minutes, not 1.8. Twelve temps would treat a symptom and would be slower still.

Rules out the CRM release. AHT after the October 9 patch (October 10–24) matches October 3–9. The jump started October 3, not October 2. Hold and after-call work, where screen slowness would also show, are flat. Rolling back the CRM is not the fix.

Rules out the floods. Flood claims are only about 11% of calls, and motor-only calls, which are unrelated to the floods, rose by the same amount. A mix shift can't produce a uniform +1.8 minutes across call types.
